verses.zh: （以东人多益来告诉扫罗说：大卫到了亚希米勒家。那时，大卫作这训诲诗，交与伶长。）勇士啊，你为何以作恶自夸？　神的慈爱是常存的。
verses.en: For the music director, a well-written song[NOTE:1] by David. It was written when Doeg the Edomite went and informed Saul: “David has arrived at the home of Ahimelech.”[NOTE:2] Why do you boast about your evil plans,[NOTE:3] O powerful man?God’s loyal love protects me all day long.[NOTE:4]
notes: Psalm 52. The psalmist confidently confronts his enemy and affirms that God will destroy evildoers and vindicate the godly.

The meaning of the Hebrew term מַשְׂכִּיל (maskil) is uncertain. The word is derived from a verb meaning “to be prudent; to be wise.” Various options are: “a contemplative song,” “a song imparting moral wisdom,” or “a skillful [i.e., well-written] song.” The term occurs in the superscriptions of Pss 32, 42, 44, 45, 52-55, 74, 78, 88, 89, and 142, as well as in Ps 47:7.

According to the superscription, David wrote this psalm during the period when Saul was seeking his life. On one occasion Doeg the Edomite, Saul’s head shepherd (1 Sam 21:7), informed Saul of David’s whereabouts (see 1 Sam 21-22).tn Heb “when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul and said to him, ‘David has come to the house of Ahimelech.’”
Heb “Why do you boast in evil?”

verses.zh: 你的舌头邪恶诡诈，好像剃头刀，快利伤人。
verses.en: Your tongue carries out your destructive plans;[NOTE:1] it is as effective as a sharp razor, O deceiver.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the loyal love of God [is] all the day.” In this context, where the psalmist is threatened by his enemy, the point seems to be that the psalmist is protected by God’s loyal love at all times.
Heb “destruction your tongue devises.”

verses.zh: 你爱恶胜似爱善，又爱说谎，不爱说公义。（细拉）
verses.en: You love evil more than good,lies more than speaking the truth.[NOTE:1] (Selah)
notes: Heb “like a sharpened razor, doer of deceit.” The masculine participle עָשָׂה (ʿasah) is understood as a substantival vocative, addressed to the powerful man.

verses.zh: 诡诈的舌头啊，你爱说一切毁灭的话！
verses.en: You love to use all the words that destroy,[NOTE:1] and the tongue that deceives.
notes: Or “deceit more than speaking what is right.”

verses.zh: 神也要毁灭你，直到永远；他要把你拿去，从你的帐棚中抽出，从活人之地将你拔出。（细拉）
verses.en: Yet[NOTE:1] God will make you a permanent heap of ruins.[NOTE:2] He will scoop you up[NOTE:3] and remove you from your home;[NOTE:4] he will uproot you from the land of the living. (Selah)
notes: Heb “you love all the words of swallowing.” Traditionally בַּלַּע (balaʿ) has been taken to mean “swallowing” in the sense of “devouring” or “destructive” (see BDB 118 s.v. בָּלַע). HALOT 135 s.v. III *בֶּלַע proposes a homonym here, meaning “confusion.” This would fit the immediate context nicely and provide a close parallel to the following line, which refers to deceptive words.
The adverb גַּם (gam, “also; even”) is translated here in an adversative sense (“yet”). It highlights the contrastive correspondence between the evildoer’s behavior and God’s response.
Heb “will tear you down forever.”
This rare verb (חָתָה, khatah) occurs only here and in Prov 6:27; 25:22; Isa 30:14.

verses.zh: 义人要看见而惧怕，并要笑他，
verses.en: When the godly see this, they will be filled with awe,and will mock the evildoer, saying:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from [your] tent.”

verses.zh: 说：看哪，这就是那不以　神为他力量的人，只倚仗他丰富的财物，在邪恶上坚立自己。
verses.en: “Look, here is the man who would not make[NOTE:1] God his protector.He trusted in his great wealthand was confident about his plans to destroy others.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and the godly will see and will fear and at him will laugh.”

The imperfect verbal form here draws attention to the ongoing nature of the action. The evildoer customarily rejected God and trusted in his own abilities. Another option is to take the imperfect as generalizing, “[here is the man who] does not make.”

verses.zh: 至于我，就像　神殿中的青橄榄树；我永永远远倚靠　神的慈爱。
verses.en: But I[NOTE:1] am like a flourishing[NOTE:2] olive tree in the house of God;I continually[NOTE:3] trust in God’s loyal love.
notes: Heb “he was strong in his destruction.” “Destruction” must refer back to the destructive plans mentioned in v. 2. The verb (derived from the root עָזַז, ʿazaz, “be strong”) as it stands is either an imperfect (if so, probably used in a customary sense) or a preterite (without vav [ו] consecutive). However the form should probably be emended to וַיָּעָז (vayyaʿaz), a Qal preterite (with vav [ו] consecutive) from עָזַז. Note the preterite form without vav (ו) consecutive in the preceding line (וַיִּבְטַח, vayyivtakh, “and he trusted”). The prefixed vav (ו) was likely omitted by haplography (note the suffixed vav [ו] on the preceding עָשְׁרוֹ, ʿoshro, “his wealth”).
The disjunctive construction (vav [ו] + subject) highlights the contrast between the evildoer’s destiny (vv. 5-7) and that of the godly psalmist’s security.
Or “luxuriant, green, leafy.”

verses.zh: 我要称谢你，直到永远，因为你行了这事。我也要在你圣民面前仰望你的名；这名本为美好。
verses.en: I will continually[NOTE:1] thank you when[NOTE:2] you execute judgment;[NOTE:3] I will rely on[NOTE:4] you,[NOTE:5] for your loyal followers know you are good.[NOTE:6]
notes: Or, hyperbolically, “forever and ever.”
Or, hyperbolically, “forever.”
Or “for.”

Heb “you have acted.” The perfect verbal form (1) probably indicates a future perfect here. The psalmist promises to give thanks when the expected vindication has been accomplished. Other options include (2) a generalizing (“for you act”) or (3) rhetorical (“for you will act”) use.
Or “wait on.”
Heb “your name.” God’s “name” refers here to his reputation and revealed character.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT
PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has
one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Notice this Psalm is addressed to wicked people (use of COLLECTIVE SINGULAR).
Most Psalms are addressed to God.

- This Psalm is a series of strophes that contrast the plight of the wicked with the security of the righteous.

- Notice it is the speech of the two groups that reveals their hearts (motives, cf. Matt. 12:34-37).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: PSALM 52:1-4
1Why
do you boast in evil, O mighty man?
The
lovingkindness of God endures all day long.
2Your tongue devises
destruction,
Like a sharp
razor, O worker of deceit.
3You
love evil more than good,
Falsehood
more than speaking what is right. Selah.
4You love all words that
devour,
O deceitful
tongue.

52:1 This is antithetical parallelism (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY, III. A. #2). Throughout the Psalm the
wicked and the righteous are contrasted (JPSOA).

The LXX makes the whole verse refer to the "wicked." The second
line has "of lawlessness all day long." AB (p. 11) makes the
second line sarcasm, "O devoted of El."

▣ "boast" This VERB (BDB 237, KB 248, Hiphil
IMPERFECT) in the Hiphil stem is often used of self praise (cf. 1 Kgs. 20:11;
Ps. 49:6; Prov. 20:14; 27:1; Jer. 49:4). In Jer. 9:23-24 the term has both negative (false boasting)
and positive (true grounds for boasting) aspects.

▣ "O mighty man" This is one
of three VOCATIVES used to describe wicked people.

- O mighty man – BDB 150, they are mighty in their boasting about their sin; this is biting sarcasm

- O worker of deceit – BDB 793 I CONSTRUCT BDB 941 I

- O deceitful tongue – BDB 546 CONSTRUCT BDB 941; not the same root as #2,
but very close (i.e., personified evil speech, cf. Ps. 1:3; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN SPEECH)

▣ "lovingkindness" This is the special covenant NOUN used
to describe YHWH's loyalty to His promises. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed).

▣ "all day long" This
denotes an extended period of time (i.e., forever; this concept must be related to context, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ['olam]). The concept of "forever"
is repeated several times in this Psalm.

- God's judgment – Ps. 52:5a

- the righteous' trust in God's lovingkindness – Ps. 52:8b

- the righteous' thanksgiving to God – Ps. 52:9a

52:2 We need to remember that words matter.
They can bless or curse (cf. James 3:1-12). There is power in words (cf.
Ps. 52:4). We will give an account to God for our words (cf. Matt.
12:34-37). Speech reveals the heart.

52:3 These are shocking parallel lines of
poetry. Just think how far humans made in the image and likeness of God (cf. Gen. 1:26-27)
have fallen (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANAKIND)! They have become polar opposites of
what they were intended to be!

The word "love" (BDB 12) is used twice in shocking ways.

- they love evil more than good, Ps. 52:3

- they love all words that devour, Ps. 52:4

▣

NASB
"than speaking what is right"

NKJV, Peshitta
"than speaking righteousness"

NRSV
"than speaking the truth"

TEV
"than truth"

NJB
"to unrightness"

JPSOA
"to speaking truthfully"

REB
"than truthful speech"

LXX
"than speakiing justice"

The reason there is such variety in the translations is because this is an
unusual use of "righteousness" (BDB 841). It is often used in
the sense of "right" (cf. Ps. 23:3) but here in the sense of
"true" (cf. Ps. 58:1). Remember, context, context, context determines word meaning.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "Selah" See Introduction to the Psalms, VII. B. #1.

52:4 "devour" This NOUN (BDB 118 I, KB 135 I) basically means
to swallow and is used as an image for destruction. KB 135 supposes that the same root might mean "confuse,"
which the NET Bible suggests fits this context best.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: PSALM 52:5-7
5But
God will break you down forever;
He
will snatch you up and tear you away from your tent,
And uproot you from the land of the
living. Selah.
6The
righteous will see and fear,
And
will laugh at him, saying,
7"Behold,
the man who would not make God his refuge,
But trusted in the abundance of his
riches
And was
strong in his evil desire."

52:5-7 This strophe contrasts what God will
do with the wicked and the response of the righteous.

- God's actions toward the wicked result in their death.

- He will break (lit. "pull down") them down forever – BDB 683, KB 736, Qal
IMPERFECT

- He will snatch up – BDB 367, KB 363, Qal IMPERFECT; this
is a rare word only here in the Psalms, but note its other three occurrences refer to "fire
taken to oneself," cf. Prov. 6:27; 25:22; Isa. 30:14

- He will tear you away from your tent – BDB 650, KB 702, Qal IMPERFECT

- He will uproot them from the land of the living — BDB 1057, KB 1658, Piel
PERFECT with waw (opposite of the faithful follower in Ps. 1:3)

- The reaction of the righteous to God's acts of judgment:

- will see – BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT

- will fear (i.e., repent in awe; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR [OT]) – BDB 431, KB 432, Qal IMPERFECT

- will laugh at their judgment – BDB 965, KB 1315, Qal IMPERFECT

(1) God laughs in Ps. 2:40; 37:13

(2) personified wisdom laughs in Prov. 1:26

(3) here the righteous laugh when the judgment of God falls on those who have rejected
Him and persecuted them. They

"laugh" in the sense of they reap what they sowed"
(cf. full lists of texts online in Gal. 6:7-16). Justice defeats injustice!

52:5 This imagery of "tear you away
from your tent" is an idiom related to the days of Israel's past (Patriarchs nomadic and later the Exodus).
This same imagery can be seen in

- Saul – 1 Sam.13:2 (i.e., to your homes)

- Sheba – 2 Sam. 20:1 (i.e., to your homes)

- Jeroboam I – 1 Kgs. 12:16; 2 Chr. 10:16 (i.e., to our own country)

- Paul – 2 Cor. 5:1-10 (tent as metaphor for the human body)

▣ "forever" The concept of
"forever" is mentioned in the Psalm's three lines.

- God's judgment is "forever," Ps. 52:5 (BDB 664, cf. Job 4:20; 14:20; 20:7; 23:7; Ps. 9:7)

- God's blessing is "forever and ever," 52:8

- forever – BDB 761 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER)

- ever – BDB 723 I (compound of them both in Ps. 9:5; 10:16; 21:4; 45:6,17; 48:14; 104:5; 119:44; 145:1,2,21)

- faithful followers' thanksgiving is "forever," Ps. 52:9 – BDB 761

▣ "the land of the living"
This CONSTRUCT (BDB 75, BDB 313) is an idiom
for life (cf. Job 28:13; Ps. 27:13; 116:9; 142:5; Isa. 38:11; Jer. 11:19).
It is in contrast to "the land of the dead," which would be Sheol
or the Pit (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?).

▣ "Selah" See note at Psalm
3:2 and Intro. to Psalms, VII. B. #1.

52:7 Psalm 52:7 is a description of the person
referred to in Ps. 52:1-4.

- he would not make God his refuge (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE)

- he trusted in the abundance of his riches, cf. Job 31:24-28; Ps. 49:6-9; Prov. 11:28; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: WEALTH

- he was strong in his evil desire (NASB)

▣

NASB
"evil desire"

NKJV
"wickedness"

NJB
"made himself strong by crime"

NRSV
"his wealth"

LXX
"powerful by his vanity"

Peshitta
"boasted in his possessions"

JPSOA
"his mischief"

The UBS Text Project, p. 255, says this root means "the riches acquired to the
damage of others." It also notes that the same root appears in v. 2a, where it is translated "destructive
plans" or "plots." This connotation fits the NASB translation.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: PSALM 52:8-9
8But
as for me, I am like a green olive tree in the house of God;
I trust in the lovingkindness of God
forever and ever.
9I
will give You thanks forever, because You have done it,
And I will wait on Your name, for it
is good, in the presence of Your godly ones.

52:8-9 As Ps 52:5 characterized the wicked
person (i.e., uprooted), Ps. 52:8 characterizes the righteous person (i.e.,
planted, cf. Ps. 1:3).

- He is like a green olive tree in the house of God, cf. Ps. 1:3;
92:12-14; 128:3; Jer. 11:16; 17:5-8.

- He trusts in God's lovingkindness forever, cf. Ps. 13:5

- YHWH's lovingkindness is forever, cf. Ps. 52:8

- the wicked "trust" in their own riches

- He gives thanks to God forever – BDB 392. KB 389, Hiphil
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense.

- He will wait on His name – BDB 875, KB 1082, Piel IMPERFECT used
in a COHORTATIVE sense.

52:8 "forever and ever" The MT has "forever and ever" (BDB 761 and BDB 723 I). The LXX
has "forever, even forever and ever." This is a way to denote "permanency."

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

52:9 "Your name" It is
characterized as "it is good" (BDB 373 II). See

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH.

The Hebrew root, "good," "pleasant," "agreeable," has a wide semantic field. Here, it is
used of God's character which issues in "lovingkindness." His creation was pronounced "good" in Gen. 1:31
because God Himself is good (cf. 1 Chr. 16:34; Ezra 3:11; Ps. 25:8; 27:13; 31:19; 33:5; 34:8; 100:4-5; 107:8-9;
119:68; 145:5-7; Nahum 1:7; Mark 10:18).

NKJV, NRSV, NJB, Peshitta

REB

This could refer to

- faithful followers at the temple (cf. Ps. 52:8, "house of God")

NRSV, Peshitta, TEV

The MT has "I will wait for" (BDB 875, KB 1082, Piel in a COHORTATIVE
sense). However, the connotation of "proclaim" fits the parallelism best (JPSOA).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the
major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought
provoking, not definitive.

- What is unusual about this Psalm?

- List the different VOCATIVES used to describe or personify the wicked.

- Compare what God will do to the wicked versus the righteous in Ps. 52:5-6.

- What do the wicked do that alienates them from God?

- Who are "the godly ones" of Ps. 52:9?
